scope: Corollary 7.4 (Coarse site features) of the manuscript “The joint Dickman law for consecutive integers” (preprints/The-joint-Dickman-law-for-consecutive-integers-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 012 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e66b4e8a1fe197d3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 55-56. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the chosen coarse partition, define Vl(S) = 1 |Il| Psplit(xb ∈ Il | S). 55 Then 0 ≤ Vl ≤ |Il|−1, and for every g ∈ L2(ΩB) the coarse value of Pm1 ug on Il is exactly E[g(S)Vl(S)]. In particular the bounds (7.2)–(7.3) and this identity hold uniformly when g varies with a position, with B, or with an external parameter.
